newsitem.title: USA: US FDA proposes speeding up new drug use approvals.
newsitem.headline: US FDA proposes speeding up new drug use approvals.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration on Thursday said it had proposed a New Use Initiative to speed up development of new and supplemental uses of medications by using all available data to determine the effectiveness of drugs and biological products.

"The science of drug development and clinical evaluation has evolved so significantly that we now have more ways to determine the benefits and side effects of new drugs," an FDA release quoted its Lead Deputy Commissioner Michael Friedman as saying, adding the initiative simplifies the approvals process while continuing to uphold standards.
The FDA said the initiative gives guidance on when the agency can determine that a drug is effective for a new use without requiring data from two new clinical trials.

It said that in some cases, a drug's effectiveness can be extrapolated from existing efficacy data, that it can be shown by evidence from a new single trial supported by existing related clinical data, or that it can be documented by adequate evidence from a single multi-center study.
